QUOTE: It splits the code on the 0xFF80 mask. The high-level bits (module, e.g. SSL, X.509, PK) go to `mbedtls_high_level_strerr()`. The low-level bits (e.g. AES, BIGNUM, ASN.1) go to `mbedtls_low_level_strerr()`... If both halves are present, the output is `high : low`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that a code has a high-level module part and a low-level part, and that mbedtls_strerror outputs both joined as "high : low" when both are present.
